newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Airline tax may have minor impact.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Airline tax may have minor impact.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said the airline ticket tax proposal from the House would cut the U.S. airline industry's 1998 pre-tax by 1.4 percent, while the Senate proposal would lower pre-tax earnings by 4.5 percent.
-- said airline stocks have underperformed the market by 11 percent over the past three weeks, which may indicate that the ticket tax issue may have been overplayed.
-- said at current levels, "we'd be looking for opportunities to accumulate airline stocks in anticipation of easier" financial comparisons for the second half of 1997.
-- said AMR Corp will be affected the most by both versions of the bill.
-- said US Airways Group Inc is "virtually unaffected," and may see a slight benefit from the House version.
-- said Southwest Airlines Co will see an impact in line with other carriers under the House bill, but is "virtually unscathed" by the Senate bill.

-- The two tax proposals have complicated formulas, but both would increase taxes on the industry. Industry analysts said the House proposal is seen as a fairly uniform bill becasue it would affect all airlines regardless of size. The Senate version, however, is seen hurting airlines with large international operations the most because it adds a 10 percent tax on the domestic portion of an international trip.
